title: Shortbread
subtitle: Scottish butter biscuits with a sandy, crumbling texture
excerpt: Three-ingredient Scottish shortbread made with a high ratio of butter to flour, pressed into a round, marked into wedges, and baked low and slow until barely golden. Simple, precise, and perfect.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shortbread is a Scottish biscuit that has been made in Scotland since at least the twelfth century, evolving from a sweetened, twice-baked bread (Medieval biscuit bread) into the all-butter shortbread known today. The word short in shortbread refers to the high fat content that gives the biscuit its characteristic crumbling, sandy texture: the fat shortens the gluten strands and prevents the biscuit from being chewy or tough. The classic recipe uses only three ingredients: butter, caster sugar, and flour in the ratio 1:2:3 by weight. Some recipes substitute a portion of the flour with rice flour or cornflour to produce an even sandier texture. The traditional Scots way to shape shortbread is as a round, pressed with the fingers at the edge, marked with a fork, and cut into wedges (petticoat tails) after baking. Shortbread Fingers are the rectangular commercial form. Baking at a low temperature is essential: the butter, which has a lower smoke point than most fats, must not colour before the biscuit is set.

recipeTools.notes: A baking tray lined with baking parchment.

content.text: The butter must be at room temperature: cold butter will not rub in smoothly and will leave a lumpy dough. Do not over-work the dough after the flour is added: the shortbread should be just brought together and pressed, not kneaded. The biscuit is done when it is a very pale gold at the edges and feels just set in the centre: it firms up significantly as it cools. Dust with caster sugar immediately on coming out of the oven.

items.preparation: or replace with plain flour for a less sandy texture

content.text: Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and smooth. Sift in the flours and salt. Mix with a wooden spoon until the mixture begins to clump. Use your hands to bring it into a ball. Do not knead.

Press the dough into a round about 20 cm in diameter on a lined baking tray. Pinch the edges neatly. Prick all over with a fork. Mark into 12 wedges with a knife without cutting all the way through. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until very pale gold at the edges.
Dust with caster sugar while still hot. Re-cut the wedge marks. Leave to cool completely on the tray before lifting: shortbread is very fragile when warm.
